entities.name: Pius III
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pope Pius III (Francesco Todeschini Piccolomini, 1439–1503) reigned only twenty-six days in 1503, one of the shortest pontificates in history. Nephew of Pius II, he was a seasoned cardinal and administrator elected as a compromise after the death of Alexander VI, when Cesare Borgia’s power and French–Spanish rivalry over Naples made a longer, stronger pope seem dangerous to many electors.

Ill at election, Pius III attempted modest curial calm and distance from Borgia excess before dying, opening the way to Julius II. His fleeting reign reveals conclave politics more than personal programme: the Sacred College briefly preferred a Piccolomini caretaker to another warrior-pope or Borgia restoration.

Pius III is remembered less for acts than for the structural crisis his election tried—and failed—to freeze.
